annotation.title_clean: Cloud First Policy (Approach to New Emerging Technologies)
annotation.title_en: Cloud First Policy (Approach to New Emerging Technologies)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Supreme Council for Information and Communication Technology (SCICT) / General Directorate of Governance and Operations, iGA, Kingdom of Bahrain
annotation.summary_en: Bahrain's 2017 Cloud-First policy requires government entities to evaluate and use cloud services for new ICT procurement. It sets security, data classification, backup, audit and role requirements for SCICT, ICTGC and iGA. It does not address AI or robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Government entities must use cloud services for new or replacement ICT unless an alternative is shown to be more cost-effective and equally secure.
Cloud providers must meet international security standards such as ISO 27001, SOC 1/2, PCI DSS and CSA.
Agencies must classify data and maintain backup and mitigation plans, with backups in a second location.
ICTGC oversees and audits compliance; SCICT approves the policy and sets strategy.
Non-restricted government data should be made open where feasible.
